content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I have two [product_name], one manages lighting, the other controls shutter movement. The [product_name] Web Editor app is loaded onto the SD card of the lighting controller. Lighting can be operated, but the shutters fail to respond when commanded—none of the related relays activate. To enable communication, I set up a network project linking the devices with flags (see attachment 1.png). All functions work except the shutter controls on the app. For shutters, I implemented push buttons in mouse HOLD mode, using block type M matched to the relevant flag.
The screenshot indicates you have a [product_name] version [version_no]. Have you enabled S7 access in the device’s properties? Path: File > Properties > Offline settings > General. [IMAGE]
I’ve enabled S7 access on both controllers; Modbus access is left disabled.
That’s why I specifically indicated S7 access should be marked. Has it started working now?
I will test this in the next few days. Should I enable both S7 and Modbus access, as shown in picture 2.jpeg?
Modbus access should only be enabled if you require communication with Modbus-compatible devices.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is unable to control shutters linked to a second [product_name] through the [product_name] Web Editor app, although lighting on the first [product_name] works without issue. Network flag configuration appears correct and lighting control is functional. Discussion centers on whether S7 or Modbus access permissions in software settings are affecting communication and remote operation reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects seamless control of shutters from the same [product_name] Web Editor app used for lighting, with reliable communication and flag-driven commands between the two [product_name] controllers.
